# Feature: Resilient Browser Interaction

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-030
**Source**: Plan Feature agent (self-contained — no plan file)

Make `yantra do` complete ordinary web forms reliably on sites nobody has ever tuned for, by fixing three things the tools get wrong today: they **misreport successful work as failure**, they **give up where one more bounded attempt would land**, and they **describe every failure with the same sentence**, so the agent learns nothing and abandons the site.

The motivating evidence is run `20260827T045106Z-do-9a58de7e` (flight search, DFW↔SJC, December 2026). It burned 12.6 minutes and 29 turns, failed 8 of 12 fill/click attempts, and published a Brief admitting it never set the destination or the dates. Every failure traces to engine mechanics, not to missing knowledge about any particular website:

| #   | Call                                     | Reported                  | What was actually true                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 10  | `fill_form` "Where from?" = `DFW`        | `WIDGET_NOT_COMMITTED`    | **The fill had worked.** The observation at seq 9 shows the combobox holding `value: "Dallas"`. The verifier compares the committed value against the _typed_ text by substring, so `"dallas"` vs `"dfw"` read as failure. |
| 14  | `fill_element` "Where else?"             | `WIDGET_ELEMENT_REPLACED` | Recovery was exhausted, then the model was told to "retry the same call once" — costing a turn to redo work the tool could have done inline.                                                                               |
| 18  | `fill_form` "Where to?" = `SJC`          | `WIDGET_NOT_COMMITTED`    | Same verifier, plus a fixed 1.5 s suggestion wait against a remote autocomplete.                                                                                                                                           |
| 22  | `fill_element` "Where to?"               | `FORM_FIELD_AMBIGUOUS`    | Two interactables named "Where to?" — the page field and the copy the open picker mounts. **The same logical control.** The resolver refuses rather than ranking.                                                          |
| 40  | `fill_form` "Choose date" = `2026-12-02` | `WIDGET_NOT_COMMITTED`    | The accessible name contains "date", so `dateInputDriver` typed into a non-typeable calendar trigger. There is no fallback to `calendarDriver`, which pages months and would have reached December.                        |
| 54  | —                                        | `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`        | Soft budget (80 % of 15 min) spent almost entirely on recovering from the above.                                                                                                                                           |

The model's own session log is the proof of cost. Turn 3: _"The origin field got into a partial state ('FW' suggesting Fort Wayne)"_ — a dropped leading keystroke nothing verifies. Turn 4: _"Origin is now set to Dallas (DFW)"_ — it worked that out **by hand from a raw observation, because the tool had told it the fill failed.**

After this feature: a widget that resolves `DFW` to `Dallas` returns success saying so; a field that drops a keystroke is retyped inside the call; a duplicate trigger resolves instead of erroring; a date field that cannot be typed into falls through to the calendar; and every failure names what was already attempted and what to do next.

**Non-goal, and the hard constraint on every line of this work:** no website-specific logic. See §2 → Spec-Specific Overrides.

## 2. Technical Context

> Standing rules (TypeScript strictness, ESM, DI, testing, logging, security) are in `.spec-lite/memory.md`. Only additions and overrides appear here.

### Approach

One new core module — `packages/core/src/interaction/` — holding the reusable primitives, consumed by the fill engine (`packages/core/src/fill/`), the widget drivers (`packages/core/src/widgets/`), and the agent's `browser_click` tool. Nothing new is invented at the tool seam; the tools get thinner as the core gets more capable.

**A. Bounded retry with an attempt ledger** (`interaction/attempt.ts`). Every outcome is classified _transient_ (element replaced, stale ref, hidden, popup not yet rendered, uncommitted-and-page-still-settling) or _terminal_ (date disabled, value invalid, ambiguous choice, mapping unsafe, host mismatch, budget). Only transient retries, within a per-call deadline and backoff. Every attempt is recorded, so a final failure can report **what was already tried** — retiring today's `"Retry the same call once"` hint, which spends an agent turn on work the tool should have finished.

**B. Stability-based waiting** (`interaction/settle.ts`), replacing the fixed `REACTION_WAIT_MS = 1_500` in [react.ts:10](../../../packages/core/src/fill/react.ts#L10). Poll the candidate list and proceed once it has been unchanged across consecutive polls, or the deadline hits. This fixes both halves of the suggestion problem: a remote autocomplete that answers late, and the current code accepting whatever list is on screen — frequently the stale list from earlier keystrokes, the likeliest source of "FW → Fort Wayne".

**C. Verified text entry with an escalation ladder** (`interaction/typing.ts`). Read the field back after typing; when the readback is a truncation of the request, escalate through generic rungs — triple-click overtype → clear + slower per-key typing → native value setter plus a real trailing keystroke. Bounded; the rung that worked is recorded.

**D. One ranked element resolver** (`interaction/resolution.ts`). Three near-duplicate implementations exist today: [`resolveFormField`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/form-field-resolve.ts), `resolveField` in [engine.ts:461](../../../packages/core/src/fill/engine.ts#L461), and the ref-matching half of `clickCandidate` in [candidates.ts:150](../../../packages/core/src/widgets/option/candidates.ts#L150). Unify them, and add a **tie-break ladder applied inside the winning tier, before ambiguity is declared**. The ladder's last rung is the safety property: _entries that tie are resolved by document order only when they share a normalized name **and** role_ — i.e. they are copies of one control. "Check-in" and "Check-out" differ in name, never reach that rung, and still fail as ambiguous exactly as today. Two controls both named "Where to?" with role `combobox` do reach it, and resolve.

**E. The disclosure contract** — the highest-value change. Verification today asks _"does the committed value contain what I typed?"_, which is the wrong question whenever a widget resolves a request to something it actually offers. When the value came from the widget's **own offered list**, the committed value is authoritative and the result says how it got there:

```jsonc
{
  "ok": true,
  "driver": "typeahead",
  "requested": "DFW",
  "committed": "Dallas",
  "resolution": "single_offered_match",
  "offered": ["Dallas"],
  "note": "The widget offered one match for \"DFW\" and committed \"Dallas\".",
}
```

The substring check against typed text survives only on the plain-text path, where nothing was offered. Failures get the same treatment — `attempted[]`, `observed`, `offered[]`, and a cause-specific next step — ending the four-identical-messages-for-four-different-causes problem the run demonstrates.

**F. Confidence-ordered driver selection with fallback.** [engine.ts:100-140](../../../packages/core/src/fill/engine.ts#L100) hardcodes one driver per detected shape and stops when it fails. Replace with an ordered candidate list built from each driver's `detect()` confidence, falling through on a not-recognized / not-committed class of failure. `dateInputDriver.detect` additionally returns 0 for a control that cannot be typed into (`readOnly`, or `aria-haspopup` in `{dialog, grid, listbox}`), which routes a picker trigger to the calendar driver first; the fallback chain is the safety net for when detection is still wrong. `createDefaultWidgetRegistry()` and `typeaheadDriver` are **currently dead code — nothing in production imports them**; this wires them in rather than leaving two divergent typeahead implementations to drift.

**G. Agent guidance** goes in the `do` profile addendum and the tool descriptions — never the system prompt, per memory (the governed prompt stays output-shape agnostic and carries no tool mechanics). The addendum is **restructured, not extended**: much of its present bulk explains mechanics the results will now report for themselves, and it is replaced with a compact result-reading contract.

**Budget.** The per-call widget budget in `defaultWidgetBudget` goes 15 s → 25 s (still well inside the 45 s `perToolTimeoutMs`) to fund retries and adaptive waits. `maxActions` goes 24 → 32. The run wall-clock budget stays 15 min — confirmed with the user: retries are paid for per call, and fewer failed turns should make runs finish sooner overall, not later.

### Spec-Specific Overrides

**New standing rule, recorded in `.spec-lite/memory.md` → General during this planning session and repeated here because it constrains every task:**

> **Never write website-specific logic.** No branch, heuristic, selector table, wait tuning, or driver hint may key off a particular site, brand, or host. Everything works from generic structural signals — ARIA roles, accessible names, widget shape, observed DOM state. A site name appearing in code is a bug; the correct fix is a more general pattern. Site names may appear in **comments and test fixture rationale** as evidence for why a general rule exists, never as a condition the code evaluates.

TASK-009 makes this mechanically enforced rather than aspirational, via an ESLint rule in the established `no-restricted-syntax` + boundary-fixture pattern.

Two smaller overrides:

- **`WidgetPort` gains `clear(ref)` and `type(ref, text, options?)`.** The typing ladder needs real key events it cannot express through `fill()` alone. This is an internal pre-release API, which memory permits breaking cleanly; every implementation (`browserWidgetPort`, the jsdom test ports) is updated in the same task.
- **`PROMPT_VERSION` is deliberately NOT bumped.** `AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT` text is untouched, so persisted prompt hashes stay interpretable. `tool_catalog_hash` will change, and the manifest already records it.

## 3. Data Model (Granular)

N/A — no relational data model, no persisted entities, no schema migration. `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does not exist and is not needed.

The durable shapes this feature defines are the **tool-result contracts**, which are recorded per call in each run's `tool-calls.jsonl` and are the agent's only view of what happened. They are stated here because their stability matters:

**`AttemptRecord`** (`interaction/types.ts`) — one entry per attempt, carried in results as `attempted[]`:

- `attempt` (number) — 1-based ordinal
- `strategy` (string) — what was tried (`"overtype"`, `"clear-then-type"`, `"native-setter"`, `"driver:date-input"`, `"driver:calendar-grid"`, `"re-resolve-ref"`)
- `errorCode` (string \| null) — null on the attempt that succeeded
- `elapsedMs` (number)
- `detail` (string, optional) — one short clause, no site names

**`FillResolution`** (`fill/types.ts`) — a closed union describing how `committed` relates to `requested`:

- `"exact"` — committed equals requested
- `"single_offered_match"` — the widget offered exactly one match; it was committed
- `"selected_from_offered"` — several were offered, one ranked uniquely; it was committed
- `"typed_literal"` — nothing was offered; the typed text stands
- `"reformatted"` — the site rewrote the value (input mask, normalization)

**`FillSuccess`** gains `requested`, `resolution`, `offered?` (≤ 10 labels), `note?` (one plain sentence), `attempted?`. **`FillFailure.details`** gains `attempted`, `observed` (the control's current committed value), and `offered` where known.

- [ ] **Implementation**: Create `packages/core/src/interaction/{types,attempt,settle,index}.ts`.

      `attempt.ts` exports `classifyFailure(errorCode, details): AttemptDisposition` with an explicit table — transient: `WIDGET_ELEMENT_REPLACED`, `STALE_ELEMENT_REF`, `ELEMENT_HIDDEN`, `WIDGET_DID_NOT_OPEN`, `WIDGET_NOT_COMMITTED`; terminal: `WIDGET_AMBIGUOUS_CHOICE`, `WIDGET_MAPPING_UNSAFE`, `WIDGET_RANGE_INCOMPLETE`, `FILL_VALUE_INVALID`, `SECRET_HOST_MISMATCH`, `ELEMENT_DISABLED`, `OPTION_NOT_FOUND`, and anything carrying `details.reason === 'budget' | 'disabled'`. Also exports `withAttempts<T, F>(run, { maxAttempts, deadlineMs, backoffMs, classify, now, label })` returning `{ outcome, ledger }`; it stops on the first terminal failure, on deadline, or on attempt exhaustion, and records every attempt including the successful one.
      `settle.ts` exports `readWhenStable<T>(read, fingerprint, { quietPolls, pollMs, deadlineMs, minReads, now })` returning `{ value, stable, reads }` — resolves once `fingerprint(value)` is identical across `quietPolls` consecutive reads, else returns the last read with `stable: false` at the deadline.

Rungs, in order: (1) `overtype` — existing `port.fill(ref, text)`; (2) `clear-then-type` — `port.clear(ref)` then `port.type(ref, text, { delayMs: 60 })`; (3) `native-setter` — `evaluateOn` uses the prototype `value` setter for `text.slice(0, -1)`, dispatches bubbling `input`, then `port.type(ref, text.slice(-1))` as a genuine keystroke so search-as-you-type listeners fire.

A readback that differs by reformatting (longer, or containing inserted punctuation) is accepted and reported as `reformatted`, so input masks are never fought. ### TASK-006: Confidence-ordered driver selection with fallback

- [ ] **Implementation**: This is the fix for the unreachable December dates.
      Add `WidgetRegistry.detectDrivers(port, target, family)` returning every driver above `MIN_CONFIDENCE`, sorted confidence-descending with registration order breaking ties.

## 7. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: Unchanged. The secret path (`fillSecretField`) keeps its existing guarantees — host binding asserted before resolution, no readback, no suggestion discovery, buffer disposed in `finally`. The typing ladder's rungs 2 and 3 are **not** available to secrets: rung 3 would place the value in an `evaluateOn` argument, and rung 2 would read it back. `commitText` therefore takes an explicit `allowEscalation` flag that `fillSecretField` sets to `false`, and a test asserts a secret fill never escalates.
- **Error Handling**: All new failures are typed `FillFailure` / `WidgetFailure` values with stable codes — no new error classes and no new codes beyond those already in `FillErrorCode`. Every failure carries `attempted` and `observed`. Nothing is swallowed: `withAttempts` returns the _last_ failure with the full ledger attached, never a synthesized one. `classifyFailure` is total over the code union so a new code cannot be silently treated as transient and loop.
- **Logging**: `attempted[]` and `resolution` ride in the existing sanitized `tool-calls.jsonl` projection — no new sink, no new artifact. Attempt `detail` strings are bounded to one clause and pass through the same sanitizer as every model-visible payload, so a page-derived value cannot leak unredacted. Nothing new is logged at Pino level; the run directory stays the durable record.
- **Security / Privacy**: `offered[]` contains page-derived text and is capped at 10 entries, crossing user-input masking and profile sanitization like every other observation field. No new network egress, no new host reached, no change to URL provenance, the ethics gate, consent, or budgets. The widget budget rise (15 s → 25 s) stays under `perToolTimeoutMs` (45 s) so the tool-level timeout remains the outer bound.
- **Determinism / replay**: Saved-workflow replay stays LLM-free. Replayed `fill_element` steps route through the same engine and inherit the retry ladder and driver fallback, which makes replay more robust without letting a model steer it — the trace records the semantic fill, never a driver choice, so nothing model-derived enters the plan.
